general_feeling: Very interesting, but it felt a little clunky
challenges: The glasses were heavy, and it was difficult to not have them or the other sensors blocked from ambient light, but paying a little extra attention solves the issue
act_impact: going out, whether in the streets or while running. While running they are in the way, and while in the streets people look at you a lot. I have been asked if I'm wearing a camera more times than I have bothered to count
beh_adapt: I stopped minding other people. There was a lady who seemed to stare a bit disapproving of me in one of the stores I went to, so the best solution was to ignore her.
social: Many. Some were interested, others poked fun at the glasses. I even have one person at my work who they made uncomfortable even after having explained that it was not a camera
improvements: Smaller sensor, smaller frame. I don't know a lot of people who look good with a chunkier frame for their glasses, but I don't know anyone who feels like they look good with a brick of a sensor on their forehead. as for how a smaller frame would work, I would suggest trying a mechanism similar to clip on sunglasses. That way people can even us their own glasses.
change_behavior: Not quite. I tried to live my life as normally as I would have, save for ignoring strangers a bit more.
